builtin.bg.env-locale.reason: A heading introducing the LANG/LC_* block: the listed variables affect only the byte interpretation of arguments and the wording of diagnostics, which POSIX leaves unspecified. The harness pins LC_ALL=C, so there is nothing observable to assert.

builtin.bg.env-nlspath.reason: XSI-shaded: 'NLSPATH determines the location of messages objects and message catalogs'. Gated on the XSI option rather than inapplicable. The requirement locates catalogs; dash ships none and emits only built-in English diagnostics, so on this host there is no catalog for NLSPATH to point at and no observable difference to assert. Recorded as conditional so it is not mistaken for a dismissed obligation.

builtin.break.non-lexical-loop-unspecifi.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "it is unspecified whether that loop encloses the command". Whether `break n` reaches a non-lexically enclosing loop in the same execution environment is therefore not a conformance question; the lexical cases are asserted by builtin.break.exit-nth-loop and builtin.break.lexically-enclosing.

builtin.exit.invalid-n-unspecified.reason: Explicitly unspecified for an n that is not an unsigned decimal integer, equals 256, or exceeds 256 without corresponding to a signal-terminated status: "the wait status of the shell or subshell is unspecified".

builtin.export.no-arguments.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "When no arguments are given, the results are unspecified." (The -p form, which IS specified, is covered separately by builtin.export.p-output-format and builtin.export.p-output-reinput.)

builtin.readonly.application-constraint.reason: Binds conforming applications rather than the shell, and states its consequence permissively: "as it may render those utilities unable to complete successfully". Marking a built-in-manipulated variable readonly is something the application shall not do; once it does, POSIX requires nothing of the shell, so neither completing nor failing the built-in can be judged.

builtin.readonly.no-arguments.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "When no arguments are given, the results are unspecified." (The -p form, which IS specified, is covered separately by builtin.readonly.p-output-format and builtin.readonly.p-output-reinput.)

builtin.set.first-argument-hyphen.reason: Explicitly unspecified when the first argument is a lone hyphen: "the results are unspecified".

builtin.special.not-exec-accessible.reason: Permissive: the special built-ins "need not be provided in a manner accessible via the exec family of functions". Neither providing nor withholding an executable file of that name can fail.

builtin.special.term-built-in.reason: Terminology plus a permission: it fixes the word built-in and then leaves the choice open, "An implementation may choose to make any utility a built-in". The one behavioural claim it makes in passing, that special built-ins differ in error handling and in the effect of preceding variable assignments, is stated normatively and asserted elsewhere by builtin.special.error-may-abort-shell and builtin.special.preceding-assignments-persist.

builtin.trap.kill-stop-undefined.reason: Undefined behaviour: "Setting a trap for SIGKILL or SIGSTOP produces undefined results." No outcome can be non-conformant.

builtin.trap.signal-name-extensions.reason: Permissive extension: "Implementations may permit names with the SIG prefix or ignore case in signal names as an extension." Accepting or rejecting SIGINT and int are both conformant.

builtin.trap.subshell-lexical-check.reason: Permissive: "Implementations may check for the single-trap-command command substitution case using only lexical analysis", so either analysis strategy conforms.
